::: {.why}
Ten questions the whole year was designed around, and anything you cannot answer is not a failure but the reading list for the autumn, which is only true if you find out which ones they are.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Answer all ten final questions out loud without notes, and score each as fluent, slow or missing.
- Attempt the four practical items and report which you could do today.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Answer the ten questions out loud, recorded, two minutes each maximum. Score each honestly against the expectation you wrote last night, and note where the expectation was wrong in either direction, since being wrong about what you know is itself worth knowing.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Attempt the four practical items rather than assuming: a point-in-time backtest of a signal from raw data in an afternoon, Black-Scholes on a whiteboard, an unseen probability question out loud, and naming the result you are least confident in. The second and third can be done in twenty minutes today; the first is a claim you should check by actually starting the clock.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the autumn reading list from whatever you scored as missing. Three items is a good list and ten is a wish.
:::
:::

## Checkpoint

Which of the ten final questions could you not answer, and what does that tell you about where to spend September?
:::
